meta.title: Event-Driven Fleet Telemetry
meta.description: Why field patches beat Redis, where Fleet Health fan-out comes from, and the smallest architecture that fixes both.

props.title: Patch the telemetry, not the infrastructure
props.subtitle: The ingest already has the cache it needs. The expensive part is sending full state into a reactive backend that recomputes Fleet Health from raw evidence.

props.content: Use a per-SN coalescing patch buffer in the existing Node process, separate liveness from telemetry state, and subscribe Fleet Health to a materialized projection. Do not add Redis yet.

props.label: Fleet Health raw queries per boat

props.title: Architecture ruling
props.content: Keep lossless raw CAN capture. Coalesce decoded values in-process and emit only material field patches. Keep one lightweight dtuLinks heartbeat. Materialize fleetHealthCurrent and let the UI subscribe to that small projection.
props.next: Prove the patch contract with replay and negative stale/clear cases before changing production.

props.label: Current Flow
props.title: The guard sits after most of the work
props.subtitle: A three-second relay timer sends full retained state; backend materiality suppresses only the final current-state patches.

props.content:
flowchart LR CAN["Raw CAN frames"] --> Capture["Lossless capture"] CAN --> Decode["PGN decode"] Decode --> State["ctx.state
all last-known fields"] State --> Dirty["dirty = true
even when unchanged"] Timer["3-second timer"] --> Full["Build full snapshot"] Dirty --> Timer Full --> Mutation["reportTelemetryBySn"] Mutation --> Resolve["Resolve org + boat
auth + rate limit"] Resolve --> History["Position history
geofence evaluation"] History --> Guard["Late materiality guard
10-second skip / 30-second backstop"] Guard --> Current["boats + telemetry"] History --> Rules["Security + Guardian + trips
samples + behavior + alerts"]
props.caption: Current source ordering: the cadence guard protects two current-state documents, not the mutation invocation, history writes, or rule engines.

props.title: The timestamp is doing two jobs
props.content: boats.updatedAt and telemetry.at are used as both data-change timestamps and liveness clocks. That coupling is why an otherwise unchanged snapshot is forced through every 30 seconds. dtuLinks already exists to own liveness.

props.label: Runtime Evidence
props.title: The Droplet has room for a Map, not another daemon

rows.meaning: Avoid adding a local cache daemon and extra serialization.

rows.observed: 961 MiB total · 322 MiB available · no swap
rows.meaning: A per-SN Map is trivial; Redis competes with ingest and journald.
The running process already holds per-SN state and can own coalescing.
Disk is not the cache bottleneck; capture custody is the larger concern.
Hourly rotation, 5 GiB per-dir caps, 60-day retention, archive configured.
At similar density, 20 boxes project to roughly 430k mutations/day.

props.title: Fleet Health subscribes to raw evidence
props.subtitle: The query is org-scoped, but each mounted subscriber recomputes the selected org from operational tables.

props.caption: Fleet Health is lazy-loaded with its screen, not global. During first load it also starts legacy queue and trend fallbacks until the board result arrives.

props.title: Why it queries every boat
props.content:
The ranking needs every boat in the selected organization to produce honest fleet coverage. That requirement is legitimate. The implementation boundary is not: a user-facing subscription should read every boat's **small health summary**, not every boat's telemetry, alert recurrence, trend history, maintenance, bookings, trips, and snapshots.

The board query also calls `Date.now()`. Time therefore advances only when a dependency write invalidates the query—another hidden reason periodic telemetry writes appear necessary.

rows.finding: Fleet Health recomputes raw org data inside a reactive query.
rows.evidence: ~3N per-boat queries plus fixed scans; budget approaches 15,000 documents.
rows.fix: Materialize one current health row per org and boat.

rows.finding: Ingest deduplication occurs after expensive work.
rows.evidence: ingestTelemetryReport reaches 75 callees; history and domain rules run before/independent of cadenceSkip.
rows.fix: Drop empty patches immediately after auth/sanitize; route real events only.

rows.finding: Tenant composite indexes are missing on health evidence reads.
rows.evidence: alerts.by_boat_createdAt and telemetrySamples.by_boat_at read by bare boat code, then filter orgId.

rows.finding: A wall clock lives inside a subscribed query.
rows.evidence: fleetHealthBoard uses now ?? Date.now(); the result ages only when some write reruns it.
rows.fix: Persist event-time projections; use client time only for display.

rows.finding: Compatibility fallback triples first-load Fleet Health work.
rows.evidence: Board, legacy queue, and legacy trend run while board is undefined.
rows.fix: Remove fallbacks after the deployed-function compatibility window.

rows.finding: Hourly snapshotAll performs an unbounded organizations.collect().
rows.evidence: The cron schedules one snapshot mutation per organization after collecting all rows.

rows.finding: The global app provider owns too many domain subscriptions.
rows.evidence: Boats, members, alerts, custody, service, bookings, maintenance, waitlist, crew, and fuel sampling mount in LiveProvider.
rows.fix: Consolidate stable projections or mount subscriptions at owning surfaces.

rows.finding: Link heartbeat is live while its watchdog is disabled in source.
rows.evidence: The Droplet sends reportDtuLinkBySn; LINK_WATCHDOG_ENABLED remains false.
rows.fix: Verify the deployed contract, then enable the existing watcher.

rows.finding: Broad collect usage needs a dedicated pass.
rows.evidence: 187 .collect() calls across 144 indexed symbols; not every collect is a defect.
rows.fix: Run the code-only Convex reviewer across the other 35 cloud-query call sites.

props.title: Cache options: one solves the actual problem

rows.benefit: Suppresses unchanged fields before network and mutation costs.
rows.failure: State resets on restart; first post-restart report performs a full sync.
Mutation, reads, history, and rules still execute.
Consumes scarce memory and shares the same host failure domain.

rows.failure: Network, credentials, availability, serialization, and another bill.

props.title: When Valkey becomes justified
props.content: Add managed Valkey only when two or more ingest replicas must share ordering, deduplication, leases, or failover state. DigitalOcean's managed Valkey is Redis-compatible and begins at $15/month for a 1 GiB single-node cluster.

props.title: Event-driven current state, separate evidence and liveness

props.caption: Raw evidence remains complete. Operational state becomes small and event-driven. Analytics subscribes to projections, not source tables.

props.title: Patch contract
props.content:
The relay keeps `lastSent` and `pending` per SN. Unchanged fields do nothing. Changed analog values coalesce until a short quiet window or three-second maximum. Safety and discrete transitions flush immediately. `0`, `false`, and `[]` remain real changes. Stale sensors use an explicit clear contract. Process startup performs one full sync.

A pure debounce is not enough because a continuously talking CAN bus may never become quiet. The correct primitive is **debounce plus max-wait**, implemented inside the existing process.

items.title: Define telemetry patch semantics
items.description: Lock changed, clear, stale, safety-immediate, restart-full-sync, and sequence behavior with replay-backed tests.

items.title: Coalesce at services/telemetry-ingest
items.description: Reuse ctx.state; add lastSent/pending and mark dirty only when the decoded state materially changes.

items.title: Move the backend no-op boundary forward
items.description: Keep auth and validation, but return before history/rules for an empty non-event patch. Preserve backend idempotence as defense-in-depth.

items.title: Materialize Fleet Health
items.description: Write fleetHealthCurrent incrementally, replace raw board recomputation, remove legacy fallbacks, then retain bounded trend snapshots.

props.title: Fitness functions that prevent the smell returning

rows.failure: Patch comparison or liveness separation regressed.

Read bounded health summaries, not raw history
rows.failure: Projection boundary leaked back into the UI query.

rows.failure: Writes are being used as a clock or paginator.

rows.failure: Data freshness and connectivity are coupled again.

props.label: Evidence Boundary
props.title: What is proven—and what is not
Live Droplet receipt
props.claim: The existing ingest process can own field coalescing without another service.
props.evidence: One Node process already owns per-SN ctx.state; 322 MiB RAM was available, no swap existed, and 5,380 successful telemetry mutations were observed in one hour.
props.limitation: The live server is still a direct-hotfix lineage; production source parity must be restored before deployment changes.

props.title: Source trace
props.claim: Fleet Health recomputes raw evidence inside a reactive screen subscription.
props.evidence: useFleetHealthBoard calls fleetHealthBoard:board through useQuery_experimental; computeQueueDetailed reads all org vessels and per-boat telemetry, alerts, and samples.
props.limitation: The production Convex deployment was not queried with an observer role, so live read counts and function versions remain unverified.

props.title: Coverage limit
props.content: This was a scoped performance and architecture audit. Production Convex advisor/insights and the full authz readiness pass were intentionally skipped because no production observer role was used. The 187 collect calls are a review queue, not 187 proven defects.
